title: ConfigMaps and Secrets

header.html: Understand ConfigMaps; Create and consume Secrets

toc.title: Keep configuration out of the image

html:
1Keep configuration out of the image

An image should run unchanged in every environment. What differs (log level, URLs, passwords) lives in ConfigMaps (plain settings) and Secrets (sensitive values) and is handed to the Pod at start. Both are namespaced objects holding key/value pairs, and a Pod can only use those in its own namespace.

ConfigMap Secret
For settings, config files passwords, tokens, keys, certificates
Stored as plain text in data base64 in data (or plain in stringData when you write it)
Size limit 1 MiB 1 MiB
Types one Opaque (default), kubernetes.io/tls, kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson, kubernetes.io/basic-auth, kubernetes.io/service-account-token, ...

base64 is encoding, not encryption. Anyone who can read the Secret can decode it (echo cGFzcw== | base64 -d). A Secret is protected by RBAC, and optionally by encryption at rest in etcd, not by base64.

2Create them

k create configmap app-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug --from-literal=color=blue
k create configmap settings --from-env-file=app.env              # each KEY=value line becomes a key
k create configmap motd --from-file=motd.txt                     # key is the file name
k create configmap motd --from-file=message=motd.txt             # choose the key name
k create configmap site --from-file=conf-dir/                    # every file in the folder
# --from-env-file cannot be combined with --from-file or --from-literal: use two commands or two ConfigMaps

k create secret generic db-creds --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal='password=S3cret!'
k create secret generic tls-files --from-file=ca.crt
k create secret tls web-tls --cert=tls.crt --key=tls.key         # type kubernetes.io/tls
k create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=registry.example.com \
    --docker-username=dev --docker-password=pw                   # type kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson

Declarative Secret with plain text: use stringData and Kubernetes stores it encoded:

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata: {name: db-creds}
type: Opaque
stringData:
  username: admin
  password: S3cret!

Read a value back: k get secret db-creds -o jsonpath='{.data.password}' | base64 -d. A ConfigMap can also be immutable: true (it can never change and must be replaced), which saves load on the API server.

3Consume them: environment variables

containers:
- name: main
  image: busybox:1.36
  env:
  - name: LOG_LEVEL                       # one key, chosen name
    valueFrom:
      configMapKeyRef: {name: app-config, key: LOG_LEVEL}
  - name: DB_USER
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef: {name: db-creds, key: username}
  envFrom:                                # all keys at once (key names become variable names)
  - configMapRef: {name: settings}
  - secretRef: {name: db-creds}
    # prefix: DB_   (optional)

Imperative shortcut on a running Deployment: k set env deployment app --from=configmap/settings (all keys) or k set env deployment app KEY=value (a literal). A key that is not a valid variable name (it has a dash) is skipped by envFrom.

Variables are read once, at container start. A changed ConfigMap or Secret does not change them in a running container: restart the Pods (k rollout restart deployment app).

4Consume them: files

volumes:
- name: conf
  configMap: {name: app-config}            # every key becomes a file
- name: creds
  secret: {secretName: db-creds, defaultMode: 0400}
containers:
- name: main
  volumeMounts:
  - {name: conf, mountPath: /etc/app}
  - {name: creds, mountPath: /etc/db, readOnly: true}
Option Effect
mount the volume the directory gets one file per key; the old content of that directory is hidden
items: [{key: x, path: y}] mount only some keys, with new file names
subPath: default.conf on the volumeMount mount one file into an existing directory without hiding the rest (such a file is not updated later)
defaultMode: 0400 file permissions (octal)
optional: true the Pod starts even if the object or key is missing

Mounted files update by themselves, after a delay of up to a minute or two, when the ConfigMap or Secret changes (except subPath mounts). The application must re-read the file.

Mount a single key as one file in a directory that has other files:

volumeMounts:
- name: conf
  mountPath: /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
  subPath: default.conf

5Failure modes

Symptom Cause
CreateContainerConfigError the ConfigMap, Secret or key named in valueFrom does not exist (create it; the Pod then starts by itself)
Pod stuck ContainerCreating, event MountVolume.SetUp failed ... configmap "x" not found a ConfigMap or Secret volume that does not exist (without optional)
Value looks right but the app still uses the old one environment variables are not refreshed: restart the Pods
illegal base64 data a hand-encoded value with a trailing newline: encode with echo -n
ErrImagePull on a private image missing or wrong imagePullSecrets
Exam tip

. Use the imperative commands for the object and a short YAML for the Pod. To avoid indentation mistakes, generate the Pod with k run ... --dry-run=client -o yaml and add env or volumes to it.

Exam tip

. "Make the running Pods use the new value" means update the ConfigMap and restart the Deployment. Updating the ConfigMap alone is not enough for environment variables.

6Lab tasks

<!-- LABS: m09 -->

Lab 9.1: configmap env volume

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-01-configmap-env-volume)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace cfg, create a ConfigMap app-config with the keys LOG_LEVEL=debug and color=blue. Create a Pod cfgpod (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that:

  • gets the environment variable LOG_LEVEL from the ConfigMap key of the same name (not a hard-coded value), and
  • mounts the whole ConfigMap as files in the directory /etc/app.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n cfg create configmap app-config --from-literal=LOG_LEVEL=debug --from-literal=color=blue
kubectl -n cfg apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: cfgpod}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    env:
    - name: LOG_LEVEL
      valueFrom:
        configMapKeyRef: {name: app-config, key: LOG_LEVEL}
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: conf, mountPath: /etc/app}
  volumes:
  - name: conf
    configMap: {name: app-config}
Y
kubectl -n cfg wait --for=condition=Ready pod/cfgpod --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cfg exec cfgpod -- sh -c 'echo $LOG_LEVEL; cat /etc/app/color'

Lab 9.2: secret env file

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-02-secret-env-file)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace sec, create a Secret db-creds with username=admin and password=S3cret!. Create a Pod dbclient (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that gets the environment variable DB_USER from the Secret key username and mounts the whole Secret read-only at /etc/db.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n sec create secret generic db-creds --from-literal=username=admin --from-literal='password=S3cret!'
kubectl -n sec apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: dbclient}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    env:
    - name: DB_USER
      valueFrom:
        secretKeyRef: {name: db-creds, key: username}
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: creds, mountPath: /etc/db, readOnly: true}
  volumes:
  - name: creds
    secret: {secretName: db-creds}
Y
kubectl -n sec wait --for=condition=Ready pod/dbclient --timeout=120s
kubectl -n sec exec dbclient -- sh -c 'echo $DB_USER; cat /etc/db/password'

Lab 9.3: configmap from files

Domain: Environment | Points: 7 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-03-configmap-from-files)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The files ~/work/app.env (lines of KEY=value) and ~/work/motd.txt exist. In the namespace cfg, create a ConfigMap settings whose keys are the lines of app.env (use the env-file option) and a second ConfigMap motd with one key motd that holds the content of motd.txt. Then create a Pod envpod (image busybox:1.36, command sleep 3600) that loads all keys of settings as environment variables with envFrom and mounts the ConfigMap motd as files in /etc/motd.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n cfg create configmap settings --from-env-file=$HOME/work/app.env
kubectl -n cfg create configmap motd --from-file=motd=$HOME/work/motd.txt
kubectl -n cfg get cm settings -o yaml | head -12
kubectl -n cfg apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: envpod}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: main
    image: busybox:1.36
    command: ["sleep", "3600"]
    envFrom:
    - configMapRef: {name: settings}
    volumeMounts:
    - {name: motd, mountPath: /etc/motd}
  volumes:
  - name: motd
    configMap: {name: motd}
Y
kubectl -n cfg wait --for=condition=Ready pod/envpod --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cfg exec envpod -- sh -c 'echo $MODE $REGION; cat /etc/motd/motd'

Lab 9.4: registry secret

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 6 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-04-registry-secret)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace reg, create a Secret of the type docker-registry named regcred for the registry registry.example.com with the username dev and the password pw123. Create a Pod private (image registry.example.com/team/app:1.0) that uses this Secret to pull its image (imagePullSecrets). The image does not exist, so the Pod is expected to stay in ErrImagePull or ImagePullBackOff: only the configuration is checked.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n reg create secret docker-registry regcred --docker-server=registry.example.com --docker-username=dev --docker-password=pw123
kubectl -n reg apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: private}
spec:
  imagePullSecrets:
  - name: regcred
  containers:
  - name: app
    image: registry.example.com/team/app:1.0
Y
kubectl -n reg get secret regcred -o jsonpath='{.type}'; echo

Lab 9.5: config change restart

Domain: Environment | Points: 6 | Time: about 7 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-05-config-change-restart)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace cfg, the Deployment cfgapp reads the key color of the ConfigMap site both as the environment variable COLOR and as the file /etc/site/color. Change the value of color in the ConfigMap from blue to green, and make sure that the running Pods of the Deployment show green in the environment variable and in the file. Wait for the rollout to finish.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n cfg patch configmap site -p '{"data":{"color":"green"}}'
kubectl -n cfg rollout restart deployment cfgapp
kubectl -n cfg rollout status deployment cfgapp --timeout=120s
kubectl -n cfg exec deploy/cfgapp -- sh -c 'echo $COLOR; cat /etc/site/color'

Lab 9.6: secret decode

Domain: Environment | Points: 4 | Time: about 4 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-06-secret-decode)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

The Secret api-key in the namespace sec stores an API token under the key token. Write the decoded token (just the plain text, no newline needed) to ~/answers/token.txt on the host where you run kubectl.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n sec get secret api-key -o jsonpath='{.data.token}' | base64 -d > ~/answers/token.txt
cat ~/answers/token.txt

Lab 9.7: configmap subpath file

Domain: Environment | Points: 8 | Time: about 8 minutes | Status: executed and validated on Kubernetes v1.37.0 (id m09-07-configmap-subpath-file)

Context: kubectl config use-context kind-ckad

In the namespace cfg, the ConfigMap proxy holds an nginx server configuration under the key default.conf. Create a Pod gateway (image nginx:alpine) that mounts only that key as the single file /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf (use subPath, so that the other files of the directory stay). When the Pod is Ready, an HTTP request to it must return the text configured.

Reference solution (try the task first; on the exam ssh <node> replaces the lab's docker exec):

kubectl -n cfg apply -f - <<'Y'
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata: {name: gateway}
spec:
  containers:
  - name: nginx
    image: nginx:alpine
    volumeMounts:
    - name: conf
      mountPath: /etc/nginx/conf.d/default.conf
      subPath: default.conf
  volumes:
  - name: conf
    configMap: {name: proxy}
Y
kubectl -n cfg wait --for=condition=Ready pod/gateway --timeout=120s

<!-- /LABS -->

7Recall questions

R1Are Secret values encrypted?

Show the answer

No; they are base64 encoded. Protect them with RBAC and encryption at rest.

R2What is the difference between env with configMapKeyRef and envFrom?

Show the answer

configMapKeyRef takes one chosen key; envFrom loads all keys as variables.

R3Does an environment variable from a ConfigMap change when the ConfigMap changes?

Show the answer

No; only after the Pod restarts. Mounted files do update.

R4How do you mount one key of a ConfigMap as a single file in an existing directory?

Show the answer

Mount the volume with subPath: <key> and mountPath set to the full file path.

R5Which command creates a ConfigMap whose keys come from the lines of a KEY=value file?

Show the answer

kubectl create configmap <name> --from-env-file=<file>.

R6What does CreateContainerConfigError mean?

Show the answer

A referenced ConfigMap, Secret or key does not exist.

R7Which Secret type holds registry credentials, and which Pod field uses it?

Show the answer

kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson (create it with docker-registry); the Pod's imagePullSecrets.

R8How do you read a Secret value on the command line?

Show the answer

kubectl get secret <name> -o jsonpath='{.data.<key>}' | base64 -d.

Quick Reference Card

Topic Remember

Env valueFrom.configMapKeyRef / secretKeyRef; envFrom for all keys
Files volumes.configMap / secret; items, subPath, defaultMode, readOnly
Refresh env: restart the Pods; files: updated by the kubelet (not subPath)

Same namespace a Pod only sees ConfigMaps and Secrets of its own namespace
